uncited: It differs from sibling methods like [Dynamic Resolution Adaptation](2683-dynamic-resolution-adaptation.md) by relying on biological gaze data rather than temporal frame budgets.
It is distinct from [Dynamic Frame Rate Adaptation](8221-dynamic-frame-rate-adaptation.md) as it maintains a constant frame rate by reducing spatial fidelity rather than temporal fidelity.
- Eye-tracking data providing the fovea position on the display.
- A composite image with high resolution in the foveal region and lower resolution in the periphery.
- **Object Points:** A list of all object points $o_i$.
- **Sub-hologram Width ($w$):** A parameter defining the resolution of the calculation grid.
- Upscale the low-resolution peripheral data to match the high-resolution center dimensions.
If $T$ is time and $w$ is width, $T \propto w^2$.
Reducing $w$ outside the fovea reduces $T$ significantly.
- **Transition Band Width:** Not given in the sources.
By reducing $w$ in the periphery, total computation time is reduced.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing both high-res and low-res buffers plus blending weights.
A variant that applies foveated resolution reduction to volume data.
It differs from point-based foveated rendering by handling volumetric density rather than discrete points.
Choose when rendering volumetric scenes with eye-tracking.
